messages:
incident-bot: ALERT Sev2 - spike in 5xx on serving-s2 across eu-west-1
Jake (oncall): seeing it, taking the page. what's the impact? approximate request failure rate?
Priya: from logs it's ~12% 5xx for the last 5m. errors look like `KVCache::miss + timeout` and `rpc_pool exhausted`
Jake (oncall): ok can we triage to model-serving runtime or infra?
Mei: infra - the pool went to 100% connections on a subset of hosts. rolling restarts started 2m ago
Jorge: rolling restarts by autoscaler? might be flapping due to liveness probe timeouts
Priya: I see a change in seq_len distribution at the same time -> longer sequences + bigger KV usage
Alex: quick mitigation: force autoscaler to hold new scale downs and add a short maintenance window. can someone create a Grafana silence so we stop paging while we stabilize?
Jake (oncall): I'll create a silence for related alerts for 30m but keep paging for DB/host-critical ones. which alert names exactly?
Mei: `serving_s2_5xx_rate > 5%` and `serving_s2_conn_exhaustion` in datadog
Jake (oncall): creating silence now for `serving_s2_5xx_rate` and `serving_s2_conn_exhaustion` - 30m
observability-bot: Silence created: ID abc123, scope: service:serving-s2, duration: 30m :white_check_mark:
Alex: thanks. parallel action: Priya can we revert the recent runtime change? or roll back quantization flags that increased memory
Priya: rolling back `quant_config.v2` on the cluster. patch applied to 3 nodes, monitoring
Jorge: adding temp bump for connection pool max to 2x to drain backlog - applied via feature-flag on infra group
Mei: host metrics trending down for CPU and connection queue, 5xx dropping to ~3% now
Jake (oncall): good. starting to think about follow-up: we should tune alerts so small transient spikes don't page on new seq_len workloads
Alex: agree. proposal: change `serving_s2_5xx_rate` from threshold 5% over 5m to 7% over 10m, and add a suppressed alert when KVcache evictions spike but 5xx remains low
Priya: also add a composite alert: `5xx_rate AND conn_exhaustion` to reduce false positives from client-side spikes
Jorge: and add a dashboard panel showing seq_len histogram + KV cache hit rate so oncall can correlate quickly
Jake (oncall): creating a ticket for alert tuning + dashboard panel. I'll own verification steps.
Jake (oncall): ticket: INF-8721 created. checklist: (1) update rules in staging (2) run synthetic long-seq traffic (3) validate that new thresholds don't mute real regressions (4) schedule maintenance-window template for planned jobs
observability-bot: INF-8721 linked to silence abc123
Alex: for validation run, let's use `loadtest-longseq` job targeting a canary pool. Priya can you run it once alert rule is on staging?
Priya: on it. will run and post results here. ETA 25m
Mei: reminder: remove the 30m silence when we're confident, and replace with a proper maintenance window for the upcoming rollout
Jake (oncall): noted. also we'll add alert annotations that show the rollout version and recent config changes to speed triage
Jorge: adding a new Grafana panel: `Seq_len vs 5xx rate (5m)` and `KV_hitrate`. PR: https://grafana.company/p/1234 - feedback welcome
Alex: lgtm. small nit: show rolling avg over 3 points so it doesn't look too choppy
Priya: test run results: synthetic longseq produced expected KV usage spike but 5xx stayed under 2% with new pool bump and rollback. logs attached: `s3://ci-artifacts/inf-8721/run1/logs`
Jake (oncall): great. I'll promote the rule to prod with the 10m window and 7% threshold after code review. anyone object?
Mei: no objections
Jorge: no objections
Alex: go ahead
Jake (oncall): prod rule updated. new rule: `serving_s2_5xx_rate > 7% for 10m` and composite condition `serving_s2_5xx_rate > 7% AND serving_s2_conn_exhaustion > 0.2` for paging
observability-bot: Prod alert rule updated: change-id rule-459-mod
Jake (oncall): lifting silence abc123 now
observability-bot: Silence abc123 ended :white_check_mark:
Priya: monitoring for 20m, 5xx staying at ~1-2%
Alex: postmortem action items: INF-8721 (alert tuning + dashboard), INF-8722 (runbook update: oncall playbook for KVcache-linked regression), INF-8723 (autoscaler liveness tuning)
Jake (oncall): I'll add owners and due dates. closing the incident then? any remaining customer impact?
Priya: we got a handful of customer errors but most retries recovered. sent an ops note to support to flag noisy customers
Jorge: let's also add a short maintenance window template in calendar for major rollouts to prevent paging; link in the ticket
Alex: thanks everyone. follow-ups in INF-8721/2/3. reconvene if anything flares. :thumbsup:
